input.paragraph_1_owner_aligned: But here’s the chicken-and-egg problem. What if you’re so far inside the child-state that you can’t become the adult? This is much easier when you can already reach one of those adult roles. But when you can't, it's like you sit there trying to be loving while your mind is becoming controlled again by the inherited critic voice, or you start going numb, throwing a fit, or panicking.
input.paragraph_2_source: I think the missing first phase is borrowed adulthood. Before you can reliably become the inner parent, you may need to experience, imagine, imitate, and practice one adult function with help. You receive care, observe how it is given, participate in it, initiate a small part yourself, and gradually internalize it.

candidate.paragraph_1: But here’s the chicken-and-egg problem. What if you’re so far inside the child-state that you can’t become the adult? But when you can't, it's like you sit there trying to be loving while your mind is becoming controlled again by the inherited critic voice, or you start going numb, throwing a fit, or panicking.
candidate.paragraph_2: Sometimes somebody else may have to do one part of the adult role with you or for you first. You get to feel what that is like and watch how they do it. Maybe you copy one small thing you've seen them do, or imagine them there when they're not, and try one piece yourself while they're still helping with the rest. That's what I mean by borrowed adulthood. You may still need help with almost all of it for a while, but over time there are more and more of those little parts you can do yourself.
